key_insight: A PICNN can replace the traditional prediction solver in a physics-preserving two-phase flow scheme while still yielding energy-stable, mass-conservative, and bounds-preserving solutions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical surrogate modeling strategy for porous-media flow simulation that is better suited than standard PINNs for local flux interactions and discontinuous permeability.
method: PICNN predicts the next-state solution using finite-volume residual training.
Interfacial fluxes are computed with TPFA and two-point difference quotients between neighboring cells.
A post-processing correction enforces thermodynamic consistency, mass conservation, and variable bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing that the finite-volume-residual-trained PICNN can successfully replace the conventional prediction solver within the physics-preserving framework.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the correction step and the ability of TPFA-based residuals to remain accurate on complex heterogeneous grids.
paper_title: The PICNN-Assisted Physics-Preserving Scheme for Thermodynamically Consistent Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media
